name: Onion Soup
description: Historical recipe from The Canadian Family Cook Book (1914). Source method; not modernized or kitchen-tested.

instructions.text: Put one tablespoonful of butter in the frying-pan
When hot add one finely chopped onion; fry it until nicely browned, being careful not to burn
Put one quart of soup stock into a stew-pan; add the fried onion and cook for fifteen minutes
Strain; return to the fire, add one tablespoonful of flour wet in a little cold water, to thicken, and boil for five minutes longer
Season with one-half a teaspoonful of salt and one-quarter teaspoonful of pepper
Cut two slices of stale bread into dice; brown the dice in the oven, put them in the soup tureen, pour the soup over them and serve at once before they become soft

source.author: Grace E. Denison
source.originalInstructions:
1. Put one tablespoonful of butter in the frying-pan
2. When hot add one finely chopped onion; fry it until nicely browned, being careful not to burn
3. Put one quart of soup stock into a stew-pan; add the fried onion and cook for fifteen minutes
4. Strain; return to the fire, add one tablespoonful of flour wet in a little cold water, to thicken, and boil for five minutes longer
5. Season with one-half a teaspoonful of salt and one-quarter teaspoonful of pepper
6. Cut two slices of stale bread into dice; brown the dice in the oven, put them in the soup tureen, pour the soup over them and serve at once before they become soft
